title: Extension along a local scheme stalk map reflects a vector bundle isomorphism
statement: Let $W,T$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $M,N$ be finite locally free $\mathcal O_W$-modules [def-sc-finite-locally-free-sheaf], let $\varphi:M\to N$, let $h:T\to W$, and let $t\in T$. Write $R=\mathcal O_{W,h(t)}$ and $S=\mathcal O_{T,t}$. If $S\otimes_R\varphi_{h(t)}$ is an isomorphism, where the stalk map is taken by [def-pc-module-stalk-functor] and extension uses the local ring map $h^\sharp_t:R\to S$, then $\varphi_{h(t)}$ is an isomorphism of $R$-modules.

source.place: Lemma 10.79.4(3), label lemma-cokernel-flat, matrix proof, applied to local rings

proof.text: Choose finite free frames near h(t); their germs identify the stalks with finite free modules of ranks m and n over R. Extension of scalars is the same matrix over S. Reduce its inverse modulo the maximal ideal of S.

The local ring map R to S induces a field extension of residue fields. Gaussian elimination shows that scalar extension of a field matrix preserves its rank. Thus m = n and the determinant is nonzero in the residue field of R. In a local ring a nonzero residue means the element is a unit. The adjugate formula gives an inverse over R. The empty matrix gives the zero-rank case.
